subject: Next steps: tool-calling integration patterns & auth options
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@anitya.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@anitya.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps: tool-calling integration patterns & auth options

Thanks again for the demo this morning — great to meet the team. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can align on an integration approach for your MVP search/retrieval and triage flow.

Goals we heard:
- Short latency retrieval (sub-200ms for embeddings-backed search) for triage UX.
- A deterministic reranker for clinical-safety heuristics (rule-based + model score).
- Ability to call external tools (scheduling, EHR lookup) from LLM responses with safe error handling and audit logs.

Proposed architecture options (high-level):
1) Single-model + tool router: Redwood hosted text-generation model with a router plugin that maps structured function calls to either EHR-call microservice or internal scheduling API. Good for fast shipping; simplest runtime.
2) Split path (preferred for safety): lightweight local reranker service (container in your VPC) for deterministic safety checks before actioning tools; Redwood model only emits candidate actions/structured JSON. This gives explicit approval gates.

Auth & SDK notes we should decide on:
- API keys (short-lived rotating) vs mTLS from private deployment. For initial MVP we recommend API keys with request-level signing; for production regulated workflows we should use Private (VPC) + mTLS.
- SDKs: we can provide the Node + Python snippets for structured tool calling and automatic retry/backoff; Sean will attach a recommended snippet.

Open questions for your team (please confirm):
- Do you want the reranker to run inside your VPC (you run the container) or as a Redwood-managed dedicated instance?
- Which systems must the tool-calling layer reach (EHR endpoints, scheduling, audit log sink)?
- Are there any strict retention rules for conversation logs > 30 days?

Next steps:
- Rajiv: confirm list of external endpoints + auth type by EOD Friday.
- Anitya: review the attached pattern doc (redwood-tool-patterns-v1.pdf).
- We'll draft a mutual action plan and a simple prototype plan for a two-week pilot.

Attachments: redwood-tool-patterns-v1.pdf (integration patterns, error handling checklist)

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — super helpful summary. Quick answers inline:

- Reranker: prefer it inside our VPC (security/compliance). We can host a Docker container.
- External endpoints: EHR read-only API (ehr-api@anitya.com), scheduling (calendar@anitya.com), and a custom audit endpoint (audit-sink@anitya.com) that requires a client certificate.
- Retention: clinical content must be retained 7 years for audit; derived prompts/summaries can be 90 days.

We'll get Rajiv to share the endpoint details and the cert requirements. Also curious about the parallel tools pattern you mentioned — would Redwood let the model call multiple tools in the same response and then do a best-of selection?

Appreciate the quick follow-up — Maria

Hi Maria — quick technical notes to clarify the parallel-tool and error-handling patterns Maria asked about.

1) Parallel tool invocation pattern (recommended for non-destructive queries):
- Model emits a structured array of tool calls with confidence scores. Example: [{"tool":"ehr_lookup","args":{...},"score":0.78},{"tool":"kb_search","args":{...},"score":0.65}]
- Redwood orchestration can fan-out those calls in parallel to your EHR and internal KB. Responses are returned to a lightweight aggregator that applies a reranker (either your container or our runtime) to pick the highest-safety candidate.
- Use-case: query enrichment where you want multiple sources for recall and then a deterministic rule/reranker to avoid unsafe suggestions.

2) Error handling & idempotency:
- Every tool call should return a status enum (ok, transient_error, permanent_error) + idempotency token.
- Transient errors trigger exponential backoff with capped retries (3 attempts) and then escalate to a human-in-the-loop or queue.
- Permanent errors should surface a safe fallback action (e.g., "ask_for_human" with a reason code) rather than returning raw model outputs.

3) Auth implications:
- For certificate-based audit endpoints: Redwood can mTLS from Private deployments. For hosted API + VPC peering, we can proxy requests through a dedicated connector with client certs stored in your KMS.
- API key rotation: we recommend short-lived keys plus HMAC-signed payloads for high-trust actions.

4) SDK snippet (Node) — pinned to our structured-calls helper (we'll attach in Drive):
- Automatic serialization of tool args to JSON Schema.
- Built-in idempotency and retry wrapper.
- Hooks for pre-call policy checks (e.g., PII redaction) and post-call audit logging.

If helpful, I can put together a small reference implementation that fans out to two mock tools (ehr + kb) so you can see the behavior with our reranker turned on/off. Jordan/Maria — want me to spin that up for the pilot?

Cheers,
Sean
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Jordan/Sean — thanks. Quick details we can share to move forward:
- EHR endpoint: https://ehr-api.anitya.com/v1/records (read-only, OAuth2 client-credentials)
- Scheduling: internal calendar API behind our auth gateway (token-based, scope: schedule:write)
- Audit-sink: https://audit-sink.anitya.com/ingest (mutual TLS required; cert will be provided via SFTP)

We can host a reranker in our VPC (Docker image) and will expose a simple HTTP scoring endpoint: /score which expects payloads <= 8KB and returns a score + reason codes. Retention and export controls will be handled by our compliance team.

We can also confirm the cert delivery and retention constraints by EOD tomorrow. Attaching the high-level endpoint matrix in this thread: anitya-mvp-map.xlsx

Regards,
Rajiv
Lead Platform Eng — Anitya Health
